question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $42,$ the additive inverse of $29$ modulo $42$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $29$ modulo $42$ is the integer $0\le x<42$ such that

$$
x+29≡0\,(\text{mod}\,42).
$$

Notice that $-29+29≡0,$ so $x≡-29\,(\text{mod}\,32).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-29 & \,(\text{mod}\,42) \\  & ≡0-29 & \,(\text{mod}\,42) \\  & ≡42-29 & \,(\text{mod}\,42) \\  & ≡13 & \,(\text{mod}\,42)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $19$ modulo $42$ is $13.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
13+29≡42≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,42)
$$

**Note:** The additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
